explanation: Russia follows Continental European table manners, where the fork stays in the left hand and the knife in the right throughout the meal — there is no cultural rule against using the left hand at the table. This differs from South Asian or Middle Eastern customs, where the left hand is considered unclean and avoided for eating.
local_tip: Hold your fork in your left hand and your knife in your right in the Continental style, rather than switching the fork to your right hand between bites as in American-style dining.

also_check.note: Eating with the left hand is considered impolite since the left hand is reserved for hygiene tasks.
The left hand is considered unclean and should not be used for eating or passing food.
Food and drink should be handled only with the right hand, as the left is reserved for personal hygiene.

sources.title: 9 Countries With Dining Etiquette Rules That May Surprise You
